item.title: Carney unveils budget to strengthen Canada's economy as Trump's trade war continues
item.description:
Carney unveils budget to strengthen Canada's economy as Trump's trade war continues
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government unveiled a sweeping budget Thursday aimed at making Canada less dependent on the United States as President Donald Trump’s trade war reshapes the longtime allies’ economic relationshipByThe Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 5:23 PM
OTTAWA, Ontario -- Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s government unveiled a budget Thursday aimed at making Canada less dependent on the United States as President Donald Trump’s trade war reshapes the allies’ economic relationship.
The budget, titled “Masters of Our Destiny,” proposes $142.1 billion Canadian (US$101.6 billion) multiyear spending and tax breaks, including incentives to attract investment and billions for energy, infrastructure and culture.
The government projects spending of $603 billion Canadian (US$431 billion) and a $62.3 billion Canadian (US$44.5 billion) deficit for 2026-27, $3 billion Canadian (US$2.1 billion) less than forecast in April.
Canada’s combined federal, provincial and local government deficits amount to 2.5% of its economy, compared with 8.5% in the United States, according to International Monetary Fund figures cited in the budget.
“The United States is upending global trade,” the budget declares.
It comes two days after Democrats swept the U.S. midterm elections, weakening Trump’s political position as the countries pursue a possible trade agreement.
The government expects Trump’s trade war to slow economic growth late this year and early next year, with the budget forecasting growth of just 1% in 2026 and 1.7% in 2027.

item.title: Bus collides with truck in eastern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people
item.description:
Bus collides with truck in eastern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people
Officials say a passenger bus has collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan, killing at least 11 people and injuring 33 othersByThe Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 1:14 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
MULTAN, Pakistan -- A passenger bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan on Thursday, killing at least 11 people and injuring 33 others, police and rescue officials said.
The crash occurred in Pakpattan district in Punjab province, said Dr. Ahmad Raza, a hospital official.
Rescuers used cranes and other heavy machinery during a three-hour operation to free passengers trapped in the wreckage, police said. Authorities declared an emergency at the hospital and called in additional doctors and medical staff to treat the injured, Raza said.

item.title: Belarus sentences Catholic priest to 3 years after he opposed the Ukraine war
item.description:
Belarus sentences Catholic priest to 3 years after he opposed the Ukraine war
A Roman Catholic priest, who has opposed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and helped Ukrainian refugees, has been sentenced to three years in prison in BelarusByYURAS KARMANAU Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 1:04 PM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
TALLINN, Estonia -- A Roman Catholic priest, who has opposed Russia's invasion of Ukraine and helped Ukrainian refugees, has been sentenced to three years in prison in Belarus, the latest move in the authorities' crackdown on critical voices, a rights group said Thursday.
A court in Belarus convicted Anatoly Parakhnevich, 66, on charges of “insulting the authorities” and “extremism” during a closed-door trial last month, said the Viasna Human Rights Center, which designated him as a political prisoner. It said Parakhnevich rejected the charges and would appeal the verdict.
Belarus' authoritarian President Alexander Lukashenko has governed the nation of 9.5 million with an iron fist for more than three decades, and Belarus has been sanctioned repeatedly by Western countries — both for its crackdown on human rights and for allowing Moscow to use its territory in the full-scale invasion of Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022.
Lukashenko’s rule was challenged after a 2020 presidential election that kept him in power, when tens of thousands of people poured into the streets to protest a vote widely seen as rigged. In an ensuing crackdown, tens of thousands of people were detained, with many beaten by police. Prominent opposition figures either fled the country or were imprisoned.
Viasna said that Parakhnevich, the parish priest in Alkovichy in northwestern Belarus, had openly opposed Russia’s war in Ukraine and condemned Belarus’ role in it, while calling for peace and repentance.

American national sentenced to life in prison for murders of partner and infant daughter in Rome

ROME -- An American man was found guilty by a Rome court Thursday of murdering his partner and their infant daughter, whose bodies were found naked in a city park, the LaPresse news agency reported. He was sentenced to life in prison.
Francis Kaufmann, 47, fled to the Greek island of Skiathos after the killings in June 2025 and was extradited by Italy to face trial for the murders of Anastasia Trofimova, 28, and their daughter Andromeda, who was nearly a year old.
Kaufmann denied killing them.

item.title: Nigerian court nullifies presidential contender’s candidacy 2 months before election
item.description:
Nigerian court nullifies presidential contender’s candidacy 2 months before election
A Nigerian court has disqualified a leading presidential candidate, complicating the electoral process two months before the electionByOPE ADETAYO Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 10:30 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
LAGOS, Nigeria -- A Nigerian court disqualified a leading presidential candidate Thursday, complicating the electoral process two months before the election.
A Federal High Court judge in Abuja, the country's capital, ruled that the leadership of the African Democratic Congress, one of the three major parties contesting the January 2027 election, was illegally constituted and therefore voided the candidacy of Atiku Abubakar.
Earlier in the year, a court ordered the party deregistered for failing to meet constitutional requirements, but an appeals court overturned the ruling. The party and government critics say the case was orchestrated by the ruling party.
Nigeria is set to go to the polls next year against the backdrop of a troubled economy and escalating insecurity. Incumbent President Bola Tinubu faces a splintered opposition, mainly from Abubakar and Peter Obi, setting up a rematch of the 2023 presidential election.
Abubakar and Obi came second and third in 2023, respectively.

item.title: Small eastern Caribbean archipelago seeking slavery reparations holds general election
item.description:
Small eastern Caribbean archipelago seeking slavery reparations holds general election
Grenada and other eastern Caribbean islands are voting in general electionsByThe Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 10:08 AM
Share
SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico -- SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico (AP) — Grenada and other eastern Caribbean islands were voting Thursday in general elections in which Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell, who has called for slavery reparations and an apology from Britain, is seeking a second term.
Mitchell, of the National Democratic Congress, faces Peter David, a former foreign affairs minister running with the Democratic People’s Movement.
Mitchell has pledged to modernize the island’s economy, strengthen healthcare services and lower youth unemployment.
He and other leaders across the Caribbean have long been pushing for an apology and reparations for slavery from Britain.
In early September, Jamaica took its case for reparations to King Charles III, and the case has since been referred to the United Kingdom’s highest court of appeal for the Caribbean island. It was an unprecedented legal maneuver, even though the British government has consistently rejected demands for either an apology or reparations.
David has promised to generate more jobs, improve medical care and create a robust local food supply system.
More than 97,000 people are registered to vote in Grenada, Carriacou and Petite Martinique.

item.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara enters liquidation phase after mandate expires
item.description:
UN's peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara enters liquidation phase after mandate expires
The U.N. peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara has entered a “liquidation phase” and is beginning to vacate positions and dispose of equipment following a U.S.-Russia standoff at the Security Council last weekByAKRAM OUBACHIR Associated Press and EDITH M. LEDERER Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 8:54 AM
LAAYOUNE, Western Sahara -- The U.N. peacekeeping mission in the disputed territory of Western Sahara will start repatriating personnel, closing a dozen facilities and disposing of equipment as part of a “liquidation phase” following a U.S.-Russia standoff at the Security Council last week.
The mission’s abrupt end after 35 years raises questions about security and stability in the region. Western Sahara is a vast desert nearly the size of Colorado and rich in fisheries and minerals. The contested resource corridor once ruled by Spain is now claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.
U.N. peacekeeping chief Jean-Pierre Lacroix said late Wednesday that the department dealing with operational issues of the U.N.’s far-flung peacekeeping missions wants to ensure an “orderly'' retreat. “And we count, of course, on the full cooperation of all the parties.”
The U.N. mission, known as MINURSO, was established in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario Front and organize a referendum on self-determination.
But the vote never materialized, as the two sides failed to agree on who would be eligible to participate. The ceasefire collapsed in 2020, and the U.N. says the region remains marked by tensions and low-intensity hostilities.
During the mission, 20 U.N. personnel lost their lives. The U.N. force was authorized to have 534 personnel, and its 2026-2027 budget was more than $62 million. The top military contributors to the force were Egypt, Ghana and Pakistan.

item.title: British man being treated for Ebola in Congo is being evacuated to the UK
item.description:
British man being treated for Ebola in Congo is being evacuated to the UK
A British man being treated for Ebola in Congo is being evacuated to the U.K., the government said ThursdayByThe Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 7:27 AM
ShareFollow ABC News on Google
LONDON -- A British man being treated for Ebola in Congo is being evacuated to the U.K., the government said Thursday.
The man, believed to be a healthcare worker, is the first British patient evacuated from the current outbreak of the deadly virus, and the third person to have tested positive to return to Europe.
The patient is expected to be taken to the Royal Free Hospital in London, which has a high level isolation unit that was used to treat patients from an Ebola outbreak in West Africa between 2014 and 2015.
The Foreign Office said the U.K.’s procedures for dealing with infectious diseases had been activated and the risk to the public from Ebola is low.

item.title: Mugabe's son faces assault charges linked to luxury car smuggling case
item.description:
Mugabe's son faces assault charges linked to luxury car smuggling case
The son of the late Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe faces assault charges after allegedly attacking an anti-corruption officialByFARAI MUTSAKA Associated PressNovember 5, 2026, 7:24 AM
HARARE, Zimbabwe -- A son of the late Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe appeared in a court in Harare on Thursday accused of assaulting an anti-corruption agency official during an operation linked to the alleged smuggling of two luxury vehicles into the country.
Bellarmine Chatunga Mugabe arrived at the Harare Magistrates Court with four other men who were arrested with him at a lodge.
Police spokesperson Paul Nyathi said Bellarmine, 29, and the four others were arrested Tuesday and face assault charges.
An anti-corruption commission spokesperson told state media Wednesday that officers had gone to the lodge to seize a Lamborghini and a Mercedes-Benz when one of the officials was assaulted. The spokesperson said the vehicles were in the country illegally.
Neither vehicle has been linked to Bellarmine, who is Mugabe’s youngest child with his second wife, Grace.
The arrest is the latest in a series of legal troubles involving members of the former president’s family in Zimbabwe and neighboring South Africa.
Bellarmine appeared in a Harare court in October on drug possession charges, but prosecutors withdrew them after his co-accused accepted responsibility for possessing cannabis.
